results.title: 6 Best Confluence Alternatives (2026) | HelpDocs
results.content:
The fix is usually a split rather than a migration. Keep Confluence as the internal wiki, where the Jira links and co-editing earn their keep, and publish the customer-facing subset of your documentation in a tool built for publishing. Your Confluence instance is untouched by this, so it isn’t a bet, and you can run both for as long as you like.

The honest cost is two tools and two bills. What you get back is an internal wiki that stays useful to engineers and a help center that’s somebody’s entire product rather than a share setting. If you’re not sure where the line falls, internal vs external knowledge base is ten minutes well spent before you book any demos.

## Moving your documentation off Confluence [...] To be fair to Confluence, it’s very good at the job it was designed for. Real-time co-editing, inline comments, page trees, genuinely strong space and page-level permissions, a Marketplace with thousands of apps, and a free plan for up to 10 users. Per-user pricing is cheap at small scale, and the Jira integration is not something you replicate with a Zapier connection and good intentions.

So, scope. This page is about replacing Confluence as a documentation and knowledge base tool, not as your team’s project workspace. If your spaces are wired into Jira, holding sprint reports, specs, and release notes that engineers actually maintain, the Atlassian integration is a real reason to stay and nothing on this list matches it. Keep Confluence for that. [...] Most teams move their core content in a few days. The sequence that works: audit your spaces and mark which pages are genuinely customer-facing versus internal only, export the ones you want to publish with their images and attachments, rebuild the structure in clean categories rather than porting the page tree, then clean up Confluence macros and restricted raw HTML and add real titles and descriptions. Point your domain at the new help center last, and keep Confluence as the internal wiki.

Thanks to Atlassian’s brilliant decisions we need to find an alternate to Confluence by February 2024 when they kill on premises server support and updates. We looked at moving to their cloud option but that is not an option due to HIPAA compliance requirements. Found out today that the Enterprise plan for the Atlassian Cloud (only option that meets HIPAA compliance after jumping through multiple hoops) has an 800 user minimum requirement.

results.title: The 10 Best Confluence Alternatives for 2026
results.content:
### What is replacing Confluence?

The most common replacements in 2026 are Slite and Notion for general team wikis, GitBook and Archbee for developer-focused documentation, and the Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace stack for teams that prefer to keep everything inside their existing productivity suite. The right replacement depends on whether the priority is AI search, non-engineering adoption, or developer workflows.

### What is the best free alternative to Confluence? [...] So, to help you on your search, here are ten Confluence alternatives we've tested in 2026, with starting price, best-fit, and where each one beats Confluence.

We've also written a deeper knowledge base software guide if you want the broader category view first.

## Why teams are leaving Confluence in 2026

If you're already shopping for an alternative, you probably recognize one of these four pains. They're the ones we hear most often from teams switching off Confluence this year.

### Rovo AI returns inconsistent results

Atlassian's Rovo is the AI layer most teams expected to fix Confluence's search. In practice, the answers come back uneven, slow, and often missing the source citations that make AI search trustworthy in the first place. [...] ## 3. Featurebase: Best for modern customer support and product feedback

Featurebase homepage

Featurebase is a modern support platform for SaaS companies that combines a help center, AI support tools, feedback collection, roadmaps, and product updates in one platform. Unlike Confluence, which mainly focuses on internal documentation, Featurebase gives support, product, and customer success teams a customer-facing platform that helps users find answers, submit feedback, and stay updated without switching tools.

It's used by SaaS companies like Lovable, Raycast, and n8n that want a cleaner alternative to managing support docs, changelogs, and feature requests across multiple disconnected products.
